subject: Hospitality
title: Event ROI Measurement
description: Learn Event ROI Measurement in one minute.

hook.text: Companies spend $500 billion annually on business events—but most can't prove the return on investment.

buildup.text: Traditional metrics include attendance, leads generated, revenue attributed, and post-event surveys.

discovery.text: Net Promoter Score (NPS) adapted for events measures likelihood to attend again or recommend.

twist.text: The most valuable event outcomes—relationship building, brand perception, employee morale.

climax.text: Event technology now tracks attendee behavior: session attendance, networking connections.

punchline.text: $500 billion spent, ROI still hard to prove. Events sell connection.

quiz.question: Why is measuring event ROI difficult?
options: The most valuable outcomes—relationships and brand perception—are hardest to quantify
